title: Attainability from both settings of a coordinate
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f\colon\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and choose a coordinate $i\notin J$ and an input $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$. Define the coordinate-polarized function $f_i^{\mathrm{pol}}$ by taking, at an input $z$, the maximum of $f$ at the two inputs obtained by setting coordinate $i$ to $1$ and $-1$ if $z_i=1$, and their minimum if $z_i=-1$. If $f_i^{\mathrm{pol}}$ can attain $-1$ at an input agreeing with $x$ with coordinate $i$ set to $1$, and agreeing with that input outside $J$, then $f$ can attain $-1$ from inputs with coordinate $i$ set to $1$ and with coordinate $i$ set to $-1$, in both cases allowing changes only in $J$ from the corresponding input.
hypotheses_covered: The polarized function can attain $-1$ from the input with coordinate $i$ set to $1$, allowing changes only in $J$
